goal: Reduce whack-a-mole gate retry loops on vague-expression guardrails (complete-context, unambiguous-requirements) by changing the gate AI reviewer to enumerate ALL violations exhaustively in a single FAIL output, and reinforcing per-phase document scan in the plan-phase author-side fix instruction. Scope is limited to the structured guardrail-article evaluation in src/flow/lib/run-gate.js. The change is uniform across all guardrail articles, but explicitly does NOT touch the requirement-implementation check (buildImplCheckPrompt) nor the post-impl markdown review (review.js / run-review.js / run-test-result-review.js). The plan-phase author-scan reinforcement (B) is added only to gate.md / gate-draft.md (gate-impl.md retains its diff-only fix discipline).

analysis.problem: complete-context (loops in 14/216 specs, max 6 iter) and unambiguous-requirements (loops in 4/216 specs, max 4 iter) frequently retry the gate because the AI reviewer cites only one example violation per FAIL, the author fixes only the cited example, and the next iteration cites a different example in the same document. The current evaluation schema in src/flow/lib/run-gate.js (GUARDRAIL_EVAL_SCHEMA, lines 619-638) returns a single `reason: string` per guardrail, structurally inviting partial citation. The same schema object is reused for the implementation-requirement check (buildImplCheckPrompt at run-gate.js:1283-1299) — semantically different (one PASS/FAIL per requirement, not 'list violations of this rule'). A naive schema change would cross-impact requirement checks; the design must split. The shared parser entry point parseEvaluationResponse(rawResponse, knownIds) is also called by both paths. Verified that run-review.js and run-test-result-review.js do NOT use this schema or parser — they have their own schemas.
analysis.proposedApproach: Combine two complementary fixes. (A) Schema/parser/prompt change in run-gate.js: introduce a guardrail-article evaluation schema that requires a `violations: [{ target, where, why_violates }]` array on FAIL (>=1 entry, all three fields non-empty for instance-level violations; document-level violations also include all three fields with `target` as a gap descriptor and `where` as the artifact name). The implementation-requirement check uses a separate, unchanged schema (renamed IMPL_REQUIREMENT_EVAL_SCHEMA). The current parseEvaluationResponse is split into parseGuardrailArticleEvaluation(rawResponse, knownIds) and parseImplRequirementEvaluation(rawResponse, knownIds); each preserves the existing known-id invariants (reject unknown / duplicates / missing). The article path enforces FAIL→violations and PASS/SKIP→reason. The article prompt instructs exhaustive enumeration: ONE violation entry per occurrence/edit location; for inherently document-level guardrails the reviewer emits one OR MORE entries (multiple distinct document-level gaps each get their own entry). The schema and prompt builder are exported by name (buildGuardrailArticleEvalPrompt, GUARDRAIL_ARTICLE_EVAL_SCHEMA) to enable direct unit tests. (B) Plan-phase author-side scan instruction in gate.md / gate-draft.md only: the instruction enumerates which artifact fields to scan per phase. gate-impl.md keeps its existing diff-only fix discipline.
analysis.validation: (A) addresses the structural cause (single-reason output → partial citation) by requiring exhaustive enumeration with target+where+why_violates per entry — duplicates are distinguishable by `where`. Splitting schemas and parser entry points isolates guardrail-article eval from requirement-impl eval. Deriving `reason` summary on FAIL preserves existing consumers (jaccard, applyFlipOverride, buildGateReport, appendIssueLogFromGateResult) without invasive refactors. The persisted issue-log keeps its current shape (entry.reason text + flat failedEvaluations[]); cross-iteration comparison granularity is unchanged in policy (reason → reason). (B) hedges residual reviewer misses with cheap per-phase wording listing concrete fields. Confirmed: only run-gate.js uses the affected schema/parser; run-review.js and run-test-result-review.js are unaffected by inspection.

qa.question: Should the change apply to all guardrail articles uniformly, or only to vague-pattern guardrails (complete-context, unambiguous-requirements) via a meta flag?
qa.answer: Apply uniformly to all guardrail-article evaluations through the article schema. The prompt rules describe two shapes within that schema: (1) instance-level guardrails — one violation entry per occurrence/edit location; (2) document-level guardrails — one OR MORE entries, each with a distinct gap descriptor as `target` and the artifact name as `where`. The implementation-requirement check uses a separate schema (IMPL_REQUIREMENT_EVAL_SCHEMA) preserving the current single-reason shape — uniform across requirement entries, not affected by this change. No per-guardrail meta flag.
qa.evidence: src/lib/guardrail.js loads guardrails uniformly with no behavioral metadata beyond phase/category/scope/lint. src/presets/base/guardrail.json has no enumerate flag. run-gate.js:1283-1299 buildImplCheckPrompt currently shares the schema with the article path — splitting at the schema/parser boundary isolates the change.
qa.why: Issue #319 names two guardrails by example, but the structural fix lives in the shared evaluation pipeline. A per-guardrail flag defers the benefit and adds metadata churn. Splitting article-eval vs requirement-impl-eval limits blast radius without per-guardrail gating.
qa.considered: Per-guardrail meta.enumerate flag — rejected for complexity. Hard-code two guardrail ids — rejected for brittleness.

qa.question: How are the schemas split, what is the parser API, what is the parsed shape, and how is malformed output surfaced?
qa.answer: Two schemas and two parser functions. (1) GUARDRAIL_ARTICLE_EVAL_SCHEMA: per-entry {guardrail_id, result, reason?: string, violations?: [{target, where, why_violates}]}. All three violation fields are required in the inner object schema; outer reason and violations are both optional in the JSON Schema (provider permissiveness — no oneOf). (2) IMPL_REQUIREMENT_EVAL_SCHEMA: identical to today's per-entry {guardrail_id, result, reason}. Parser API: parseGuardrailArticleEvaluation(rawResponse, knownIds), parseImplRequirementEvaluation(rawResponse, knownIds). Both preserve existing known-id invariants (reject unknown / duplicates / missing). Article parser additionally enforces FAIL→violations[] >=1 with non-empty target/where/why_violates per entry, and PASS/SKIP→non-empty reason without violations field. On any violation of these invariants the parser throws EvaluationSchemaError with a message identifying the offending entry and field. The gate command catches the error and emits an envelope with errors[0].code = 'EVALUATION_SCHEMA_ERROR'; the gate retry counter increments (one slot consumed). The user-facing prompt instructs the AI fixer to either retry (if budget remains) or surface to the user. On FAIL article entries the parser writes a derived `reason` summary (joined '<target> — <why_violates>' with '; ' separator) onto each FAIL entry; downstream consumers read it without code changes. Persisted artifacts: in-flight data.artifacts.evaluations stores parsed shape (violations[] retained on FAIL article entries); issue-log persists entry.reason text + flat failedEvaluations[] only.
qa.evidence: Current single schema run-gate.js:619-638; current parser run-gate.js:728+ enforces unknown/duplicate/missing checks (lines 760-786); reasonsFromEvaluations run-gate.js:1380; buildGateReport run-gate.js:800-820 requires reason; applyFlipOverride run-gate.js:1263-1276 reads e.reason; assertNoRepeatedFail run-gate.js:1189-1234 reads c.reason / p.reason; appendIssueLogFromGateResult run-gate.js:1960 stores text reason + flat failedEvaluations[].
qa.why: Splitting schemas and parser entry points removes cross-impact with requirement-impl checks. Permissive provider schema avoids oneOf reliance. Parser-thrown EvaluationSchemaError is the existing error path; reusing it preserves the gate envelope contract. Counting schema errors in the retry budget prevents a runaway loop on a malformed-output bug.
qa.considered: Single parser with mode parameter — rejected: branching inside parser confuses invariants. Single schema with conditional/oneOf — rejected for provider compatibility. Excluding schema errors from retry budget — rejected: would let a deterministic schema bug exhaust resources.

qa.question: What fields does each violation entry carry, what is the operational standard for 'exhaustive enumeration', and how are duplicates distinguished?
qa.answer: Entry: {target: non-empty string, where: non-empty string, why_violates: non-empty 1-2 sentence string}. All three are REQUIRED. For instance-level violations: `target` is a verbatim text excerpt; `where` is a heading anchor, JSON dotted path, or file:line reference that uniquely locates the occurrence. For document-level violations: `target` is a short gap descriptor (e.g. 'missing section: Acceptance Criteria'); `where` is the artifact name (e.g. 'spec.md', 'draft.json'). Standard: ONE violation entry per occurrence/edit location for instance-level. Repeated occurrences of the same vague phrase in different places are distinct entries because each requires a separate edit; they are distinguishable by `where`. Literal duplicates with the same `target` AND same `where` are forbidden by parser uniqueness rule applied per (guardrail_id, target, where) triple — duplicates raise EvaluationSchemaError. Document-level guardrails: ONE OR MORE entries — emit a separate entry for each distinct document-level gap. The parser does not enforce 'exhaustiveness' (it cannot know what was missed); per-occurrence is enforced via prompt wording and a regression fixture asserting that a fixture with two distinct vague phrases yields two violations.
qa.evidence: Issue body iter examples (e.g. complete-context iter 3 'should 項目 3 つ' = three should items, each with distinct surrounding text) call out repeated occurrences. The reviewer pointed out that without required `where`, identical-target entries are ambiguous.
qa.why: Required `where` makes every entry uniquely actionable. Multiple document-level entries prevent over-collapsing (different document-level gaps are independently fixable). Per-occurrence enforcement is naturally aligned with author edits.
qa.considered: Optional `where` — rejected: ambiguous duplicates. Single document-level entry only — rejected: hides multiple gaps. Use a discriminator field (instance_kind) — rejected: complexity for marginal benefit.

qa.question: What is the persisted issue-log shape and why is violations[] not added to it?
qa.answer: issue-log shape is unchanged. appendIssueLogFromGateResult continues to write `entry.reason` (text summary), `failedEvaluations[]` (flat `{guardrail_id, reason}` derived from buildFailedEvaluations), and `passedGuardrails[]`. Violations[] is NOT persisted to issue-log. Justification: issue-log's primary cross-iteration consumer is assertNoRepeatedFail's jaccard pipeline, which operates on text strings; the derived FAIL `reason` already incorporates every violation's target+why_violates as a single string, so jaccard's input grows in fidelity automatically. Adding violations[] to issue-log would require schema migration and adapter code in jaccard / no-progress / flip-override paths for marginal benefit. If finer-grained cross-iteration analysis is needed in the future, that is a separate spec.
qa.evidence: run-gate.js:1960 appendIssueLogFromGateResult — entry.reason is a string; failedEvaluations from buildFailedEvaluations (run-gate.js:1156-1166) returns `{guardrail_id, reason}` per FAIL. run-gate.js:1118 JACCARD_THRESHOLD = 0.5. run-gate.js:1128 normalize tokenizes reason string.
qa.why: Derived reason in issue-log scales naturally with violation count without schema changes. Keeping persisted shape stable avoids cross-spec migration concerns.
qa.considered: Extend issue-log to persist violations[] — rejected: out of scope and requires migration. Switch jaccard to compare violations[] sets — rejected: out of scope and risks behavior drift in spec 210's no-progress guard.

qa.question: What are the test cases and what test seams (exports) are required vs indirect?
qa.answer: Required new exports (must export for direct unit tests): GUARDRAIL_ARTICLE_EVAL_SCHEMA, IMPL_REQUIREMENT_EVAL_SCHEMA, parseGuardrailArticleEvaluation, parseImplRequirementEvaluation, buildGuardrailArticleEvalPrompt. Indirect (no new export needed): reasonsFromEvaluations is tested via gate command envelope output (data.artifacts.reasons); applyFlipOverride / assertNoRepeatedFail / buildGateReport are already exported. Test list and priorities: (must) (1) GUARDRAIL_ARTICLE_EVAL_SCHEMA shape unit tests (FAIL/PASS/SKIP); (must) (2) parseGuardrailArticleEvaluation rejection — FAIL with empty violations, missing violations, target/where/why_violates empty, PASS with violations, SKIP without reason, unknown id, duplicate id, missing id, duplicate (guardrail_id, target, where) triple; (must) (3) parseGuardrailArticleEvaluation derives reason summary on FAIL — exact derived string asserted; (must) (4) gate envelope test (mocked agent): FAIL with two violations → data.artifacts.reasons has two FAIL rows with correct rendering; (must) (5) buildGuardrailArticleEvalPrompt text — exhaustive-enumeration directive, document-level guidance with example, section ordering; (must) (6) parseImplRequirementEvaluation regression — same outputs as old parseEvaluationResponse on requirement-style inputs; (should) (7) gate envelope on malformed output — agent returns FAIL with empty violations[] → envelope errors[0].code === 'EVALUATION_SCHEMA_ERROR', retry counter incremented; (should) (8) Jaccard regression with constructed low-overlap fixture (assertNoRepeatedFail does NOT throw) and high-overlap fixture (DOES throw); (should) (9) applyFlipOverride regression — prior PASS, current FAIL article entry, derived reason — flip applies. Exact test file paths will be enumerated in the spec phase task list. All tests use mocked agents or pure-function inputs.
qa.evidence: Existing exports list at run-gate.js:1948+; existing testable exports (parseEvaluationResponse, EvaluationSchemaError, normalize, jaccard, applyFlipOverride, assertNoRepeatedFail). The schema and prompt builder are currently internal.

qa.considered: Test only via the public envelope (no new exports) — rejected: schema and prompt structure are first-class behaviors and tests via envelope hide failure modes. Export every internal helper — rejected: enlarges public surface for marginal benefit.

qa.question: Does the diff-scope constraint (DIFF_SCOPED_PHASES = task-impl, integration) interact with exhaustive enumeration?
qa.answer: Yes. For diff-scoped phases, the reviewer enumerates only violations within added/modified diff lines. The current diff-scope text (IMPL_DIFF_SCOPE_LINES at run-gate.js:572-581) already restricts judgment to + lines. The enumeration directive in buildGuardrailArticleEvalPrompt explicitly states 'when diff-scope applies, list only violations introduced by the diff.' Section ordering keeps the diff-scope block AFTER the rules + schema directive so the enumeration command remains primary.
qa.evidence: run-gate.js:572-584 IMPL_DIFF_SCOPE_LINES + DIFF_SCOPED_PHASES; buildGuardrailPromptFromFiltered:678-680 conditional append.
qa.why: Inherited restriction prevents over-reporting pre-existing violations in unchanged code, which would block legitimate diffs.
qa.considered: Disable enumeration for diff-scoped phases — rejected: diff-scoped phases benefit equally from listing all in-diff violations.

qa.question: Does the previously-passed-IDs short-circuit (run-gate.js:669-676) interact with the new schema?
qa.answer: No data-model interaction. Prompt section ordering is normative: rules → schema → fmt fallback → previously-passed (if any) → diff-scope (if any) → articles → content. The schema directive (specifying violations[] on FAIL) precedes the previously-passed informational section so the reviewer cannot read previously-passed as a relaxation of the schema. A test asserts this ordering.
qa.evidence: run-gate.js:669-676 only adds an informational section. Existing buildGuardrailPromptFromFiltered uses .add() in a fixed order via PromptBuilder.
qa.why: Ordering enforcement keeps the schema directive salient even when previously-passed is present.
qa.considered: Move previously-passed before schema — rejected: weakens schema directive's salience.
